YOUR RIGHTS

Know your options
before you act.

Plain-language guidance for asking better questions. Rules vary by loan and location.

01 / BEFORE THERE IS A PROBLEM

Build confidence with the basics.

Use these ideas when reviewing an offer or checking an account. They make it easier to spot questions worth asking early.

01

APR isn’t the whole story

APR helps compare credit costs, but review every fee, whether it is financed, and the total paid over the full term.

02

Watch the clock

Extending a term may lower a monthly payment while increasing how long you are in debt and what you pay overall.

03

Keep the paperwork

Save the offer, disclosures, messages, and notes about conversations. They make it easier to check terms later.

04

Pause on pressure

Be cautious of claims that an offer expires immediately. Take time to read the disclosures and seek independent help if needed.

02 / IF A LOAN GOES TO COLLECTIONS

Start with the facts, deadlines, and records.

General U.S. consumer information—not individualized legal advice. Rules and deadlines can vary.

View guide ↓
01

Verify the contact

Ask for the collector’s name and contact information, the creditor, the account, and the amount claimed. Avoid sharing sensitive financial information until you can confirm who is contacting you.

CFPB: When a collector contacts you →
02

Review and keep records

Keep the validation notice, letters, payment records, and dated notes of calls. If you believe the debt or amount is wrong, consider disputing it in writing and review the notice for its deadline.

CFPB: Disputes and contact limits →
03

Do not ignore court papers

If you are sued, read the papers and respond by the deadline shown. Responding does not mean you agree that the debt is valid; it preserves your ability to raise issues with the court.

CFPB: If you are sued →

BEFORE YOU BEGIN

A quick legal notice

DebtShark is an educational, planning, and record-keeping tool. It is not a law firm and does not provide legal, financial, or tax advice.

  • It does not determine your legal rights, calculate legal deadlines, submit filings, or guarantee an outcome.
  • You are responsible for checking your information and meeting any deadline in a notice or court document.
  • If you receive court papers or face an urgent deadline, consider contacting a qualified lawyer or legal-aid organization promptly.

Using DebtShark does not create an attorney-client relationship.
